title: 实验证实物质波 (戴维森-革末实验)
title_en: Experimental Confirmation of Matter Waves (Davisson-Germer Experiment)

video.title: 电子像波一样行为：戴维森和革末的实验
video.title_en: Electrons act as waves : the proof by Davisson and Germer

summary.text: 克林顿·戴维森和雷斯特·革末, 在贝尔实验室工作, 为路易·德布罗意的"物质波"假说 (`de_broglie_matter_waves_1924`) 提供了决定性的实验证据. 通过向镍晶体发射电子束, 他们观察到电子并没有像粒子一样随机散射, 而是形成了一个与X射线 (波) 相同的"衍射图案". 这证实了物质 (电子) 具有波动性, 巩固了波粒二象性的概念, 并为戴维森赢得了1937年的诺贝尔奖.
summary.text_en: Clinton Davisson and Lester Germer, working at Bell Labs, provided the definitive experimental proof for Louis de Broglie's hypothesis of 'Matter Waves' (`de_broglie_matter_waves_1924`). By firing a beam of electrons at a nickel crystal, they observed that the electrons did not scatter randomly like particles, but formed a 'diffraction pattern' identical to X-rays (waves). This confirmed that matter (electrons) possesses wave-like properties, solidifying the concept of wave-particle duality and earning Davisson the 1937 Nobel Prize.
key_points: 证实了德布罗意的"物质波"假说

story.text: 这个发现部分源于一次幸运的事故. 戴维森和革末正在研究电子从镍表面的反射. 在一次实验中, 一个液态空气瓶爆炸了, 震碎了真空管并氧化了镍靶. 为了清洁镍, 他们将其加热到非常高的温度. 这个加热过程意外地将镍从许多小晶体变成了几个巨大的单晶. 当他们恢复实验时, 电子以一种奇怪的, 有峰值的图案反射, 而不是平滑的分布. 他们意识到大晶体的规则原子间距起到了电子波的"衍射光栅"的作用, 正如布拉格 (`bragg_diffraction_1913`) 对X射线所描述的那样.
story.text_en: This discovery was partly due to a lucky accident. Davisson and Germer were studying electron reflection from nickel surfaces. During one experiment, a liquid air bottle exploded, shattering the vacuum tube and oxidizing the nickel target. To clean the nickel, they heated it to a very high temperature. This heating process accidentally transformed the nickel from many small crystals into a few large, single crystals. When they resumed the experiment, the electrons reflected in a strange, peaked pattern rather than a smooth distribution. They realized the regular atomic spacing of the large crystal was acting as a 'diffraction grating' for the electron waves, exactly as Bragg (`bragg_diffraction_1913`) had described for X-rays.

fun_facts.text: 同年 (1927年), 苏格兰的乔治·佩吉特·汤姆孙使用金属薄膜独立发现了电子衍射. 他与戴维森分享了诺贝尔奖.
fun_facts.text_en: In the same year (1927), George Paget Thomson in Scotland independently discovered electron diffraction using thin metal films. He shared the Nobel Prize with Davisson.

fun_facts.text: J.J. 汤姆孙 (父亲) 因证明电子是"粒子"而获得诺贝尔奖. 乔治·佩吉特·汤姆孙 (儿子) 因证明电子是"波"而获得诺贝尔奖. 他们都是对的.
fun_facts.text_en: J.J. Thomson (the father) won a Nobel Prize for proving the electron is a 'Particle'. George Paget Thomson (the son) won a Nobel Prize for proving the electron is a 'Wave'. Both were right.

simple_explanation.text:
德布罗意说"粒子像波一样行为". 戴维森和革末验证了这一点.
他们向"水晶墙" (镍) 发射"电子" (粒子).
如果电子只是球, 它们会随机地向各个方向反弹.
但它们没有. 它们以特定的角度成束反弹, 形成了一种图案.
这正是"水波"或"光波"撞击格栅时所做的 (衍射). 这证明了固体物质像波一样运动.
simple_explanation.text_en:
De Broglie said 'Particles behave like waves'. Davisson and Germer checked this.
They shot 'electrons' (particles) at a 'crystal wall' (nickel).
If electrons were just balls, they would bounce off in all directions randomly.
But they didn't. They bounced off in specific 'beams' at specific angles, creating a pattern.
This is exactly what 'water waves' or 'light waves' do when they hit a grate (Diffraction). It proved that solid matter moves like a wave.

applications.title: 电子显微镜
applications.text: 电子像波一样衍射的事实使我们可以制造电子显微镜, 它使用电子束而不是光来看比原子还小的东西.
applications.text_en: The fact that electrons diffract like waves allows us to build Electron Microscopes, which use electron beams instead of light to see things smaller than atoms.

applications.title: 低能电子衍射 (LEED)
applications.text: 这个实验诞生了LEED技术, 今天广泛用于材料科学以研究晶体的表面结构.
applications.text_en: This experiment birthed the technique of LEED, widely used today in materials science to study the surface structure of crystals.

impact.text: 戴维森-革末实验是早期量子力学的最后一块拼图. 它将德布罗意的"物质波"从理论假说变成了观察到的现实. 它证实了量子力学定律不仅适用于光 (光子), 也适用于物质 (电子), 确立了波粒二象性的普遍性.
impact.text_en: The Davisson-Germer experiment was the final piece of the puzzle for early quantum mechanics. It moved de Broglie's 'Matter Waves' from a theoretical hypothesis to an observed reality. It confirmed that the laws of quantum mechanics apply not just to light (photons), but to matter (electrons), establishing the universal nature of Wave-Particle Duality.

influenced_by.contribution: 德布罗意 (他的"物质是波"的假说是他们正在测试的)
influenced_by.contribution_en: De Broglie (his hypothesis that 'matter is a wave' was what they were testing)

influenced_by.contribution: 布拉格 (他的X射线衍射定律提供了通过电子图案解释数学的基础)
influenced_by.contribution_en: Bragg (his law of X-ray diffraction provided the math to interpret the electron pattern)

influenced.contribution: 恩斯特·鲁斯卡 (利用电子的波动性发明了电子显微镜)
influenced.contribution_en: Ernst Ruska (used the wave nature of electrons to invent the Electron Microscope)

influenced.contribution: 薛定谔 (该实验验证了他的波动力学方法)
influenced.contribution_en: Schrödinger (the experiment validated his wave mechanics approach)

influence_chain.legacy_text: 戴维森和革末证明了即使是固体物质, 在其核心, 也是一种波.
influence_chain.legacy_text_en: Davisson and Germer proved that even solid matter is, at its heart, a wave.

quiz.question: 戴维森和革末观察到了什么现象证明电子像波一样行为?
quiz.question_en: What phenomenon did Davisson and Germer observe that proved electrons behave like waves?
quiz.explanation: 衍射是波独有的属性. 粒子随机散射, 但波干涉形成波峰和波谷 (图案). 看到电子形成图案证明了它们有波长.
quiz.explanation_en: Diffraction is a property unique to waves. Particles scatter randomly, but waves interfere to form peaks and troughs (patterns). Seeing electrons form a pattern proved they have a wavelength.
